question: Without an implant, up to how many days post-surgery can a wound infection still be called a surgical site infection?
explanation: Standard guidelines classify any infection that develops within thirty days after surgery, when no implant is left in place, as a surgical site infection. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T6#BMP120_U4_T6_h1)

question: Why do midwives and nurses need to monitor patients for surgical site infections even after they leave the hospital?

options.A: Many infections take days to develop and show signs after discharge
options.B: Midwives cannot check wound healing inside the hospital wards
options.C: Surgical bacteria only become active once the patient is outside
options.D: Patients always remove their wound dressings too early at home

explanation: Infections often need time to incubate, meaning signs and symptoms may only appear after the patient has already gone home. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T6#BMP120_U4_T6_h1)

question: Which health condition can slow down white blood cells and help bacteria grow faster in a surgical wound?
explanation: High blood sugar levels make it harder for infection-fighting white blood cells to work properly, creating an environment where bacteria thrive. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T6#BMP120_U4_T6_h2)

question: Why is a patient who has emergency surgery at a higher risk for a wound infection?

options.A: Emergency surgery requires the use of stronger local anesthetics
options.B: Emergency theatres are always kept at much warmer temperatures
options.C: The patient will automatically reject all forms of antibiotic coverage
options.D: There is no time for optimal preoperative hygiene and stabilization

explanation: Because it is an emergency, there is less time to clean the skin thoroughly or stabilize chronic health conditions before the operation. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T6#BMP120_U4_T6_h2)

question: Which sign is a clear, definite indicator that a surgical wound is infected?

options.A: Itching sensation around healing skin staples
options.C: Faint pink discoloration on the wound edges
options.D: Mild serosanguinous fluid on the dressing

explanation: Pus coming from the wound is a reliable sign that bacteria have caused an active infection. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T6#BMP120_U4_T6_h3)

question: Why do midwives sometimes draw a line around the redness on a wound with a pen?

options.A: It prevents the patient from touching the tender surgical incision
options.B: It permanently kills any bacteria living on the surface of the skin
options.C: It helps determine if the erythema is spreading or shrinking over time
options.D: It speeds up the process of applying a fresh sterile wound dressing

explanation: Drawing around the red area lets you easily check later if the redness is growing larger, which means the infection might be spreading. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T6#BMP120_U4_T6_h3)

question: Why must you clean surface crusts off a wound before taking a swab for the lab?

options.A: To stop the wound from bleeding while the transport medium is being prepared
options.B: To prevent the laboratory technician from accidentally contaminating the hospital ward
options.C: To ensure the swab collects the actual infecting bacteria rather than skin contaminants
options.D: To make the patient feel more comfortable during the diagnostic procedure

explanation: Surface crusts often carry normal skin germs that are not causing the actual infection deep inside the wound. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T6#BMP120_U4_T6_h4)

question: Which blood test result usually points to an active bacterial infection in a post-op patient?
explanation: The body makes more white blood cells to fight off invading bacteria, leading to a higher count in the lab results. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T6#BMP120_U4_T6_h4)

question: Why do doctors change a patient's antibiotics from broad-spectrum to narrow-spectrum once lab results are ready?

options.A: To ensure the patient takes fewer pills every single day of the week
options.B: To save money because narrow-spectrum drugs are always much cheaper
options.C: To target the specific germ found while reducing the risk of antibiotic resistance
options.D: To stop the patient from experiencing any side effects from strong drugs

explanation: Switching to a targeted drug treats the exact germ causing the problem while protecting the body's normal bacteria and preventing drug resistance. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T6#BMP120_U4_T6_h5)

question: What is the main reason for giving antibiotics before the lab culture results come back?

options.A: To numb the surgical incision so the patient feels no physical pain
options.B: To rapidly control suspected bacterial growth while waiting for lab results
options.C: To replace the routine practice of aseptic wound dressing changes
options.D: To permanently eliminate the need for any future surgical wound care

explanation: Starting medications early helps fight off likely bacteria right away while everyone waits for the final lab report. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T6#BMP120_U4_T6_h5)

question: What is the main goal of surgical debridement for an infected wound?

options.A: Removal of necrotic and infected tissue to promote healing
options.B: Injecting local anesthetic drugs deep into the muscle layers
options.C: Stitching the skin tightly closed to stop any further bleeding
options.D: Replacing lost blood volume with intravenous fluid infusions

explanation: Debridement clears away dead, infected tissue so healthy new cells can grow and the body can heal. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T6#BMP120_U4_T6_h6)

question: Why might a surgeon remove a stitch or two from an infected surgical cut?

options.A: To test if the skin has finished healing completely
options.B: To make room for a new adhesive plaster dressing
options.C: To reduce the patient's overall body temperature
options.D: To allow trapped pus and fluid to drain out freely

explanation: Loosening a small part of the wound relieves pressure and lets infected fluid escape, helping the patient recover faster. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T6#BMP120_U4_T6_h6)

question: What is the most important rule to follow when changing a wound dressing to keep new bacteria out?

options.A: Using clean unsterile household gloves for speed
options.B: Strict adherence to aseptic technique and hand hygiene
options.C: Warming the dressing materials before application
options.D: Applying heavy amounts of perfumed antiseptic lotion

explanation: Good hand washing and sterile techniques stop outside germs from getting into the open wound. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T6#BMP120_U4_T6_h7)

question: Why should a recovering surgical patient eat foods rich in protein and vitamins?

options.A: It completely kills any bacteria living inside the bowel
options.B: It keeps the patient's blood pressure at a normal level
options.C: It stops the patient from feeling nauseated after anesthesia
options.D: It supports strong immune function and rapid tissue repair

explanation: Proteins and vitamins give the body the building blocks it needs to fight infection and close up the wound quickly. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T6#BMP120_U4_T6_h7)
